task.description:
WF-03 Step Final (git-merge, hard gate, runs ONCE) for GH-716 / ISS-0675 / PAR-06. All prior steps complete: Step 00 (git-setup) PASS, Step 0.5/1 (ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis) PASS recommending deletion, Step 2 (CODE-DESIGNER) SKIPPED with verified rationale (pure dead-code deletion, no design content needed), Step 3 (BACKEND-DEV implementation) PASS -- deleted Store.reconstructBounded() and helpers/error variants from src/event_store/store.zig, Step 4 (TEST-DESIGNER) SKIPPED (no business logic changed), Step 5 (TEST-RUNNER) PASS -- zero regressions, full baseline match, Step 6 (RELEASE-VALIDATOR) SKIPPED (MINOR severity, not BLOCKER), Step 7 (DOC-UPDATER) PASS -- CHANGELOG updated, PAR-06 requirement status confirmed accurate (still RELEASED).

Branch feature/WF03-GH716-20260812 already has several commits pushed to origin from earlier ADHOC/TEST-RUNNER/DOC-UPDATER steps in this run (this is expected -- an earlier ADHOC step pushed slightly ahead of the normal Step Final push, but no PR was opened yet). Complete the full Step Final procedure:

1. Push the branch (including the latest Step 7 commit d43c97a7 and any commits after it) to origin.
2. Open a PR from feature/WF03-GH716-20260812 to main. Title should reference GH-716 and PAR-06. Body should summarize: what was deleted (dead code Store.reconstructBounded() and helpers), why (unreferenced duplicate of reconstruction.zig's live, tested path; wiring it up instead would have been a regression since it lacked the live path's correct empty-window fallback), test verification (zero regressions, full baseline match), and 'Closes #716'.
3. Wait for CI to complete, then run `python tools/check_github_status.py` FIRST (mandatory per core-directives.md's 'Never Call a Red Pipeline OK Without a Source') before characterizing CI as green or red. Quote its actual output.
4. If CI is green: squash-merge the PR, delete the branch (local and remote), and confirm main is up to date locally.
5. If CI is red: investigate per core-directives.md (read the failing step, determine if platform-caused or code-caused using check_github_status.py's output) and fix or report accurately -- do not merge on a red pipeline.
6. Close GitHub issue #716 with an accurate resolution comment summarizing the fix and linking the merge commit.
7. Update handoffs/global_queue.json: find the GH-716 entry (status QUEUED, lock null) and set status to RESOLVED, run_id to WF03-GH716-20260812, started_at/completed_at to real timestamps.
8. Complete this handoff and confirm the repo is back to a clean main with no stale feature branches.
acceptance_criteria: python tools/check_github_status.py run and quoted BEFORE characterizing CI result
CI verified green via actual evidence (not assumed)
main is clean and up to date after merge
GitHub issue #716 closed with accurate resolution comment
handoffs/global_queue.json GH-716 entry updated to RESOLVED with this run_id

result.summary: GH-716/PAR-06 Step Final completed with a material deviation from the dispatched task: during rebase-before-push, discovered a second, independently-dispatched pipeline instance for the identical issue had already opened and squash-merged PR #739 (commit a6490f61) at 2026-08-12T09:35:34Z, closing GH-716, ~32 minutes before this handoff was dispatched -- a duplicate-dispatch race on the shared run_id label, not a code conflict. Reconciled rather than re-merged: rebased this branch onto post-#739 main (store.zig deletion matched exactly; this branch additionally removed 2 now-unreachable StoreError variants + EventWindow struct that #739 left behind, plus design-doc/comment updates #739 did not include); preserved both runs handoff audit trails under distinct filenames (append-only, no history dropped); resolved orchestrator.log/registry.json rebase conflicts by union; removed a duplicate CHANGELOG entry. Incidentally discovered tests/integration/iss0686_archived_state_test.zig (GH-733, unrelated) was unwired in build.zig, blocking this branch own zig build test gate -- fixed inline per Unblock-Everything (wired as new addTest root matching par05_solo_tests pattern; fixed a real setup(h.conn) vs setup(&h.conn) pointer-mismatch bug in its generated boilerplate; zig fmt applied), filed and closed as GitHub #741. Could not push the rebased branch to the original feature/WF03-GH716-20260812 ref (non-fast-forward; force-push is forbidden by role file) so opened PR #742 from a fresh branch feature/WF03-GH716-20260812-final instead. All validation green: zig build / zig build check / zig build test / zig build migrate all exit 0; lint_sql_param_types.py 0 findings; test-integration-par06 3/3, test-integration-par06-reconstruction 5/5, newly-wired test-integration-iss0686 all pass against real PostgreSQL. check_github_status.py: "GitHub Actions status: operational -- platform healthy. A red run is therefore attributable to the change under test." All 8 CI checks on PR #742 passed (verified via gh pr checks and gh run view --json jobs, cross-checked against gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup). Squash-merged as 677c9829. GH-716 was already closed by #739; posted an accurate resolution comment on it documenting both the original fix and this reconciliation. handoffs/global_queue.json GH-716 entry was already RESOLVED with run_id WF03-GH716-20260812 (set by the #739 run, since both runs shared the label) -- verified accurate, no further edit needed. Both feature branches (original feature/WF03-GH716-20260812 and feature/WF03-GH716-20260812-final) deleted locally and remotely; main confirmed clean and up to date.

issues.description: ORCH dispatched two independent pipeline runs for the same GitHub issue (GH-716) under the identical run_id WF03-GH716-20260812, racing to completion; the second (this handoff) had to detect and reconcile the collision manually during Step Final. Worth a queue-locking or run_id-uniqueness check in ORCH dispatch logic to prevent recurrence.
